subject: Beta invite: Hosted canary rollouts (percentage traffic splitting) in Redwood Console
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Jensen <ava.jensen@northstar-support.ai>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@northstar-support.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@emberfin.com>, Jordan Kim <jordan.kim@emberfin.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@helpwave.io>
Date: Fri, Mar 7, 2025 at 10:08 AM PST
Subject: Beta invite: Hosted canary rollouts (percentage traffic splitting) in Redwood Console
Attachments: Hosted_Canary_Rollouts_Beta_Guide_v0.9.pdf; Hosted_Canary_Beta_Feedback_Template.docx

Hi all —

We’re inviting a small set of customers to be design partners for our upcoming GA “Hosted canary rollout workflow” in Redwood Console.

What you’ll get in the beta
- A Console workflow to canary a new model version/config on an existing Hosted route using percentage-based traffic splitting (e.g., 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%).
- Built-in guardrails: max step size and minimum soak time, optional approval gates, and auto pause/rollback on SLO breaches (error rate / timeouts / p95 latency regression).
- A rollout timeline / activity history (who changed what and when) visible in Console.
- Side-by-side baseline vs canary metrics (latency/error/throughput) to support go/no-go.

What we’re asking from design partners
- 2–3 weeks of active use on one (1) Hosted route.
- 30 min kickoff to confirm route/model/version, success criteria, and alert thresholds.
- 1x weekly 30 min check-in while the beta flag is enabled.
- Quick feedback on UX + “gotchas” (we’ll give you a template; free-form is fine too).

Beta guardrails / expectations
- Best-effort support, no SLA for beta features.
- Feature can be disabled quickly (kill switch) if we observe unexpected routing behavior.
- We strongly recommend starting with low-risk traffic and conservative stop conditions.

Enablement steps (if you want in)
Reply with:
1) Your Redwood tenant/org name (or org_id if you have it handy)
2) The Hosted route you want to canary (route name + environment)
3) Baseline model/version and the canary model/version/config you want to introduce
4) Primary region(s) you care about
5) Who should be in a Slack Connect channel for fast coordination

Once we have that, we can enable the beta flag for your tenant and schedule the kickoff.

Kickoff scheduling link: https://calendly.com/redwoodinference/hosted-rollouts-beta-setup

Thanks — if this aligns with what you’re trying to do over the next few weeks, we’d love your feedback before we lock GA behavior.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference


---

From: Ava Jensen <ava.jensen@northstar-support.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Mar 7, 2025 at 1:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Beta invite: Hosted canary rollouts (percentage traffic splitting) in Redwood Console

Hi Marissa,

Yes — this is timely for us. We’re planning a model upgrade on our support-agent route and would like to do it safely.

Details:
1) Tenant: northstar-prod (we can send org_id if needed)
2) Route: /v1/chat/support-agent (prod)
3) Baseline: redwood-llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-02-10
   Canary: redwood-llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-03-01 (different quant profile + new prompt template)
4) Regions: us-east-1 primarily, with some us-west-2
5) Slack Connect: me + Miguel (cc’ing him)

One question: for the cohorting, is the split sticky per end-user? We’d prefer to avoid users bouncing between baseline/canary.

Thanks,
Ava


---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Jensen <ava.jensen@northstar-support.ai>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@northstar-support.ai>
Date: Fri, Mar 7, 2025 at 2:04 PM PST
Subject: Re: Beta invite: Hosted canary rollouts (percentage traffic splitting) in Redwood Console

Ava (and hi Miguel) —

Perfect, thank you. We can work with that route.

Re: stickiness — yes. In the beta we use deterministic cohort assignment so a given “cohort key” stays assigned to baseline vs canary across requests while the rollout is active (so you don’t see request-to-request bouncing).

We’ll confirm the exact cohort key we’ll use with you during kickoff (common options are end_user_id, your stable customer/account id, or a hashed header value). If you don’t have a stable end-user identifier today, we can still cohort by request id, but then you won’t get user-level stickiness.

Next steps
1) Can you reply with your Redwood org_id (or a screenshot of the Console org settings page) so we enable the flag on the right tenant?
2) Please book a kickoff slot here: https://calendly.com/redwoodinference/hosted-rollouts-beta-setup
3) We’ll spin up a Slack Connect channel (#hosted-rollouts-beta) after kickoff scheduling so engineering/SRE can join.

Also: for the first run, we recommend a conservative schedule (1% for 30–60 min, then 5% for 1–2 hrs, then 25% etc.) and “auto pause” on a relatively tight 5xx/timeout threshold.

Thanks again — looking forward to partnering.

— Marissa


---

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@emberfin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Kim <jordan.kim@emberfin.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 9:11 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Beta invite: Hosted canary rollouts (percentage traffic splitting) in Redwood Console

Marissa,

Interested, but want to confirm governance/audit posture before we enable in production.

Questions:
1) Will we be able to require an approval step for moving from (say) 5% → 25%?
2) Are actions (create rollout / start / step change / pause / rollback) captured in audit logs with actor identity, timestamps, and what changed?
3) What’s the retention period for those audit events?

If those are in place, we can likely use this on a low-risk route first.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Director, Platform Engineering
Emberfin


---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@emberfin.com>
Cc: Jordan Kim <jordan.kim@emberfin.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 4:22 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Beta invite: Hosted canary rollouts (percentage traffic splitting) in Redwood Console

Priya (cc Jordan) —

Yes on (1) and (2), and we can share specifics on (3).

1) Approval gates
- In beta, you can configure a rollout to require an explicit “approve” action before progressing beyond certain steps (we typically gate higher-risk jumps, e.g., >10% traffic).
- We can also set a policy to cap max step size and enforce minimum soak time.

2) Audit logs
- Rollout actions are captured with actor identity (user/service principal), timestamps, route + rollout id, and the change (e.g., traffic split 5% → 25%, pause initiated, rollback reason = auto-stop threshold breach).
- Console also shows a customer-visible rollout timeline for quick review.

3) Retention
- Default retention aligns with your existing Redwood audit log retention tier. If you’re using our standard audit log export, events are also exportable to your SIEM.
- Let me know your target (e.g., 90d/180d/1y) and we’ll confirm what’s available for your plan and what’s in beta vs GA.

If you want to proceed, the enablement reply items in my first note apply (tenant/org, route, baseline/canary model versions, regions, Slack contacts). We can also start in staging if you’d like to validate the approval workflow and audit output before touching prod.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference
